title: On Returning to Bibhutibhushan's Aranyak
author: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay
reflection: What strikes me most about Aranyak is the absence of ideological preaching. Satyacharan's gradual intoxication with the wilderness does not make him an eco-philosopher; it makes him a deeply wounded witness to the tragedy of progress. The prose possesses a quiet Vedic grandeur.

title: The Dual Conscience in Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
reflection: Raskolnikov's real punishment is not Siberia; it is the immediate, agonizing psychological severance from other human beings the moment the axe strikes. Dostoevsky demonstrates that moral law is not social convention, but an intrinsic biological condition of sanity.

title: Tagore's Gora and the Mirage of Purity
author: Rabindranath Tagore
reflection: Gora's fanatical adherence to ritual purity is exposed when he discovers his Irish parentage. In one stroke, Tagore dismantles the entire illusion of exclusionary nationalism, showing that identity is a living, welcoming river, not a fenced stagnant pool.
